snippet.title: Build Bigger Arms In 45 Mins (Scientifically)
snippet.description:
This arm workout only took me 45 minutes. Low-volume, high-intensity. Let’s go.

First up: 2 sets of Bayesian curls. Keep your upper arm behind your body and think about stretching your biceps at the bottom of each rep. Squeeze hard at the top. Both sets to failure.

Next: 2 sets of throat crushers. Some would call these JM presses, they’re basically in between a skull crusher and a close-grip bench press: bringing the weight down to your neck. Lower the weight under control and be careful.

Then: 1 hard set of preacher curls to failure. All your focus should be on your biceps, I stay in the bottom ⅔ of the range of motion on these.

For shoulders, all I did was 2 sets of machine lateral raises. Think about sweeping the weight out rather than shrugging it up. Both sets to failure.

Next: 2 sets of cable kickbacks. Brace with your non-working hand and focus on squeezing your triceps at full extension. Both sets to failure.

Then: 1 set of inverse Zottman curls to failure. These are really fun and challenging if you haven’t tried them before! Curl up with a hammer curl grip, rotate your palms up at the top, and control the eccentric on the way down. 

To finish: 2 sets of wrist curls and 2 sets of wrist extensions! Get the full Min-Max routine on jeffnippard.com!

snippet.title: I Gained Fat Over The Holidays
snippet.description:
Over the holidays, I kind of let go. I ate whatever I wanted, my training was off and I barely tracked anything. At first I didn’t notice much, but before I knew it I was up 7 lbs, and now I feel like I’ve flattened out too. And I do feel a little bad about it. If you’re in the same spot, here’s what not to do.

First, don’t beat yourself up. Some food guilt is normal, but sitting with it doesn’t help at all. Notice it, then let it go.

Second, don’t think it was all fat. If it was only a few weeks, a lot of that weight is just water retention and food waste. So drink plenty of water, and include fruits and whole grains to help with digestion.

Third, don’t do anything extreme. No crash diets, or punishing workouts. The “damage” is never as bad as it feels in your head. Just ease back to normal. For me, that’s 45 minute workouts and roughly tracking my macros.

If you're looking to get back on track, download MacroFactor 2 weeks free (use code JEFF).

snippet.title: The Cancer Expert: "This Common Food Is Making Cancer Worse!"
snippet.description:
Dr. Thomas Seyfried isn’t just another cancer researcher. He’s a trailblazer challenging the core belief of modern oncology. While mainstream medicine treats cancer as a genetic disease caused by mutations, Dr. Seyfried argues that cancer is actually a metabolic disorder rooted in damaged mitochondria — the cell’s energy factories.
His radical idea? Cancer doesn’t begin with bad genes — it begins with broken metabolism.

In this video, we break down a powerful yet often misunderstood idea: that cancer is not primarily a genetic disease, but a metabolic one. Based on the groundbreaking work of Dr. Thomas Seyfried, we’ll explain in clear, bite-sized segments how cancer really begins—not with mutated genes, but with damaged energy metabolism in the cell. You’ll learn what fuels cancer cells to grow, and what you can do to interrupt that process. We’ll also cover practical strategies for managing and preventing cancer, including what foods to eat, which ones to avoid, and how to create an internal environment that starves cancer cells while supporting healthy ones.

snippet.title: The Craziest Fact About Human Eyes
snippet.description:
👁️🧠 Did you know your eyes are actually part of your brain? In this fascinating clip, Dr. Andrew Huberman explains how the **retina, optic nerve, central nervous system, brain function, circadian rhythm, sleep-wake cycles, and visual processing** are all deeply connected.

Most people think the eyes simply send information to the brain, but according to neuroscience, the **retina is brain tissue** that developed outside the skull during early development. 🤯 Your eyes don't just help you see—they also help regulate **alertness, sleep, hormone production, melatonin release, cognitive performance, mood, energy levels, and overall brain health**.

This short explores the science behind **vision, neuroscience, biology, brain anatomy, light exposure, circadian biology, sleep optimization, neuroplasticity, cognitive function, and human physiology**. Understanding how your eyes interact with your brain can completely change the way you think about **sunlight, blue light, sleep quality, focus, productivity, and mental performance**.

If you're interested in **brain science, health, biohacking, sleep, neuroscience, psychology, human biology, self-improvement, wellness, and longevity**, this is one of the most mind-blowing facts you'll hear all day. 🌞⚡

snippet.title: What’s Happening To America’s Food?
snippet.description:
🍟🚨 Is modern food contributing to the rise in chronic disease? In this discussion, RFK Jr. raises questions surrounding **food ingredients, processed foods, food additives, food dyes, preservatives, pesticides, public health, nutrition, and the modern food system**.

This conversation explores topics including **ultra-processed foods, chronic disease, obesity, metabolic health, inflammation, food regulations, artificial ingredients, health awareness, environmental toxins, wellness, healthy eating, food quality, preventative health, and long-term health outcomes**. 🧠🌱

As conversations around **nutrition science, clean eating, gut health, biohacking, ingredient transparency, food industry practices, and health optimization** continue to grow, more people are asking important questions about what goes into the foods consumed every day.

💡 Food isn't just calories — it's information for your body.

Three to four pasture-raised eggs per day provide one of the most nutrient-dense protein sources available.
